lines: Fields teach patience. Fights teach exactly when patience has run out.
Mud on my boots, fear in my throat, and home still ahead. I made it.
I made it back with mud on my knees and luck in both pockets.
The field path never felt so long. The village never looked so good.
I kept thinking about sunrise. That helped me keep moving.
I have weathered storms, but storms do not usually carry axes.
Home was the only crop I cared about reaching.
My boots are ruined. I am not. Good trade.
I remember the moment I realized running was no longer possible.
My hands shook afterward more than they did during the fight.
I survived because someone watched the side I could not see.
The noise made every decision feel late.
I lost track of time until the danger passed.
One good piece of cover mattered more than all my courage.
I learned how quickly a small wound can slow you down.
The first quiet breath afterward felt unreal.
I checked my gear twice before I trusted that it had held.
Fear kept me alert, but training kept me useful.
I do not remember every strike. I remember who came home.
Surviving changed which risks look worthwhile.
